definition: Domestic terrestrial fibre infrastructure: backbone, middle mile, backhaul, metropolitan rings, last-mile fibre, optical ground wire, dark fibre and supporting ducts, poles and civil works. Cross-border terrestrial links belong to submarine_cable. A last-mile fibre connection may also qualify as access_connectivity; a shared institutional fibre network may also qualify as institutional_networks. Assign overlapping labels only when each function is explicit.

Ground-based wireless communications infrastructure, including mobile radio access networks, base stations, towers, fixed wireless access, microwave links and terrestrial broadcast transmission. Includes associated site power, shelter and grounding. Explicitly targeted spectrum arrangements qualify as support to this category. Wireless last-mile connections or institutional networks may also receive their respective labels. Excludes satellite communications and generic spectrum policy without an identifiable terrestrial wireless object.

Satellite communications infrastructure and services, including ground stations, teleports, VSAT terminals and purchased satellite capacity for backbone, backhaul or user connectivity. Satellite last-mile connections may also qualify as access_connectivity. Excludes satellite imagery and earth observation, which belong to geospatial. Licensing or technical assistance qualifies only when explicitly directed at satellite communications.

International communications infrastructure and capacity: submarine fibre cables, landing stations, branching units, cross-border terrestrial links, international gateways and associated cable installation, maintenance and repair. Excludes domestic fibre routes without an international connectivity function. Satellite capacity remains satellite unless a distinct international gateway or interconnection intervention is explicitly described.

Facilities and computing services that host, store or process digital data and applications. Includes data centres, server rooms, colocation, cloud hosting, computing capacity, hosting migration, associated power and cooling, and dedicated backup or recovery environments. Retains internet exchange points within this category. Excludes hosted applications and registries themselves. Application-level backup does not imply a separate hosting investment unless a hosting facility, service or environment is identifiable.

Shared communications networks linking institutions or their internal sites and services. Includes government WANs and VPNs, research and education networks, sector networks, institutional LANs and their network operations centres. Includes shared email, voice and unified communications delivered as network services. Explicit fibre, wireless or satellite infrastructure may also receive its technology label. Last-mile connections may additionally qualify as access_connectivity; the institution being connected alone does not establish a shared network.

Dedicated capabilities that protect digital systems and data against cyber threats. Includes security operations centres, incident response teams, threat monitoring, security controls, audits and testing. Excludes incidental security features without a distinct intervention. Shared identity, digital-signature and trust infrastructure belongs to dpi; a separate cybersecurity function may also qualify. Personal-data protection alone is not cybersecurity.

Shared foundational digital systems for identity, interoperable payments, data exchange and digital trust. Includes civil registration, unique identification, payment rails, interoperability layers, digital signatures, credentials and public key infrastructure. Data protection, consent or governance qualifies only when explicitly directed at these shared foundations. Excludes generic data governance, sector registries, service portals and sector-specific applications, which are digital_systems. A separate cybersecurity intervention may also qualify as cybersecurity.

asset_name: Early warning and emergency communication systems
definition: Digital hazard monitoring, warning and emergency communications systems. Includes hydrometeorological and seismic networks, forecasting, public alert platforms, emergency call-taking and dispatch, dedicated responder networks and digitally equipped emergency operations centres. Includes sector warning systems when their warning function is explicit. Excludes generic buildings, one-off risk assessments and advisory applications without warnings. This asset category is broader than the ews measure: emergency response infrastructure does not automatically establish a warning intervention.

Last-mile connectivity and access provision for people, communities and institutions. Includes user connections by fibre, wireless or satellite; public Wi-Fi; community networks; access devices and subscriptions; and supply-side connection subsidies. Includes power or physical protection applied to identifiable access sites. Technology labels may also qualify when explicit. Excludes digital literacy, generic affordability aspirations and devices used only to operate a named sector system. Shared institutional networks qualify separately when explicit.

Digital sensing, monitoring or control of physical infrastructure and processes. Includes SCADA, smart meters, smart-grid communications, intelligent transport systems, utility telemetry and operational sensor networks. Monitoring need not directly control equipment to qualify. Standalone analytical or administrative software is digital_systems. Hazard monitoring and warning infrastructure is drm_ews; assign both only when distinct operational and warning functions are explicit.

Systems, equipment and services that capture, manage or share location data. Includes spatial data infrastructure, GIS platforms, geoportals, earth observation, aerial surveys, LiDAR, geodetic networks and base mapping. Excludes a one-off hazard map or assessment without a separately identifiable geospatial system, equipment or data service. Land and cadastre registries are digital_systems; their distinct geospatial infrastructure may also qualify.

Named sector or government applications, information systems, registries, service platforms and portals. Includes health, education, public finance, tax, customs, land, justice, statistics, procurement and agricultural advisory systems. Includes equipment explicitly supplied to operate these systems. Excludes generic hardware or software without an identifiable system; shared foundational layers are dpi, hosting is data_hosting and geospatial infrastructure is geospatial. Warning or operational-control functions may receive their specialised asset labels when separately explicit.
